views.name: matches_with_card_context
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Matches.id AS id,
  Matches.card_id AS card_id,
  Matches.winner_id AS winner_id,
  Matches.loser_id AS loser_id,
  Matches.win_type AS win_type,
  Matches.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  Matches.duration AS duration,
  Matches.title_id AS title_id,
  Matches.title_change AS title_change,
  Cards.table_id AS table_id,
  Cards.location_id AS location_id,
  Cards.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  Cards.event_date AS event_date,
  Cards.event_id AS event_id,
  Cards.url AS url,
  Cards.info_html AS info_html,
  Cards.match_html AS match_html,
  Promotions.id AS promotion_id__fk,
  Promotions.name AS name,
  Locations.id AS location_id__fk,
  Locations.name AS location_name,
  Events.id AS event_id__fk,
  Events.name AS event_name
FROM Matches
LEFT JOIN Cards ON Matches.card_id = Cards.id
LEFT JOIN Promotions ON Cards.promotion_id = Promotions.id
LEFT JOIN Locations ON Cards.location_id = Locations.id
LEFT JOIN Events ON Cards.event_id = Events.id

params.description: Row-level view of individual matches enriched with their card, promotion, location, and event context (one row per match).
params.when_to_use: Get match-level details plus the card/event/promotion/location names and ids for reporting or filtering. | Build further SQL aggregations at the match grain (for example counts, rates, or joins to wrestler-level aggregates) while preserving one-row-per-match semantics. | Compose with other dimension/look-up views to add descriptive attributes (match type name, wrestler names) or to aggregate matches into card- or event-level summaries.
params.output_schema: id: Matches.id — primary key of the match (one row per Matches.id). | card_id: Matches.card_id — foreign key referencing Cards.id for the card that contains this match. | winner_id: Matches.winner_id — foreign key referencing the wrestler who won the match (from Matches table). | loser_id: Matches.loser_id — foreign key referencing the wrestler who lost the match (from Matches table). | win_type: Matches.win_type — raw win_type value from Matches (method of victory). | match_type_id: Matches.match_type_id — id pointing to a match type lookup (from Matches). | duration: Matches.duration — match duration value as recorded in Matches. | title_id: Matches.title_id — id of the title (if any) at stake from Matches. | title_change: Matches.title_change — boolean/flag from Matches indicating if title changed. | table_id: Cards.table_id — table identifier from the joined Cards row (card-level attribute). | location_id: Cards.location_id — foreign key to Locations.id from Cards. | promotion_id: Cards.promotion_id — foreign key to Promotions.id from Cards (card-level). | event_date: Cards.event_date — event date from Cards (card-level date/time). | event_id: Cards.event_id — foreign key to Events.id from Cards. | url: Cards.url — card-level URL from Cards. | info_html: Cards.info_html — card-level info HTML from Cards. | match_html: Cards.match_html — card-level match HTML from Cards. | promotion_id__fk: Promotions.id — id from Promotions joined by Cards.promotion_id = Promotions.id (duplicate of Cards.promotion_id but denormalized here). | name: Promotions.name — promotion name from Promotions.name (promotion-level attribute). | location_id__fk: Locations.id — id from Locations joined by Cards.location_id = Locations.id (duplicate of Cards.location_id but denormalized here). | location_name: Locations.name — location name from Locations.name (location-level attribute). | event_id__fk: Events.id — id from Events joined by Cards.event_id = Events.id (duplicate of Cards.event_id but denormalized here). | event_name: Events.name — event name from Events.name (event-level attribute).
params.grounded_columns: Matches.id | Matches.card_id | Matches.winner_id | Matches.loser_id | Matches.win_type | Matches.match_type_id | Matches.duration | Matches.title_id | Matches.title_change | Cards.table_id | Cards.location_id | Cards.promotion_id | Cards.event_date | Cards.event_id | Cards.url | Cards.info_html | Cards.match_html | Promotions.id | Promotions.name | Locations.id | Locations.name | Events.id | Events.name
params.metric: This view does not define new aggregated metrics. All columns are row-level attributes taken directly from base tables. | If you need match-level derived metrics, compute them on top of this view. Example derived metric patterns you can safely compute per row: | is_title_change = CASE WHEN title_change THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | match_minutes = CAST(duration AS numeric)  -- if duration is stored as a numeric/seconds string convert accordingly | Note: No aggregate expressions are defined in this view; aggregation must be done by the consumer.
params.composition: SAFE to join (one-to-one or many-to-one into this view) without duplicating match rows/measures: |  - Join to match_type_lookup on matches_with_card_context.match_type_id = match_type_lookup.id — safe because match_type_lookup is a lookup (one row per match_type_id). |  - Join to matches_with_wrestler_names on matches_with_wrestler_names.id = matches_with_card_context.id — safe if matches_with_wrestler_names is also one-row-per-match (it is a sibling JOIN view at match grain). |  - Join to cards_with_promotion_and_location on matches_with_card_context.card_id = cards_with_promotion_and_location.id — safe if cards_with_promotion_and_location is one-row-per-card (many matches may reference the same card, but joining does not multiply matches; it attaches card attributes). |  - Join to events or promotions dimension views keyed by event_id or promotion_id (one-row-per-event or one-row-per-promotion) — safe because those are dimensions. |  | DO NOT join directly (without re-aggregation) to the following shapes because they will multiply this view's rows/measures: |  - Any one-to-many child table of Matches (e.g., a hypothetical match_participants table listing many participants per match) — joining would duplicate match rows for each child row. To compose, either aggregate the child table to match-level first or use EXISTS/IN filters. |  - Any one-to-many table keyed to Cards (for example card_images or card_attendance_by_day) if the table has multiple rows per card — joining by card_id would multiply all matches on that card by the number of child rows. Aggregate the card-side child to card-level first, then join on card_id. |  | Guidance for safe composition/aggregation: |  - To produce match-counts per card: SELECT card_id, COUNT(*) FROM matches_with_card_context GROUP BY card_id. |  - To compute wrestler-level aggregates (e.g., wins): join matches_with_card_context -> aggregate by winner_id (COUNT(*) filters for win_type or winner_id) or join to wrestler_aggregate_record which is an AGG sibling (ensure wrestler_aggregate_record is at wrestler grain). |  - If you must join a one-to-many view, perform the aggregation on that view to match-grain (or card-grain) first. For example to add number_of_card_images per card: join matches_with_card_context.card_id to (SELECT card_id, COUNT(*) AS card_image_count FROM card_images GROUP BY card_id). |  | Rationale: matches_with_card_context has grain = one row per Matches.id. Joins to true dimensions or other one-row-per-match views preserve cardinality. Joins to one-to-many child datasets will multiply match rows and therefore must be pre-aggregated or reduced to one row per Matches.id (or per card_id when joining on card) before joining.

views.description: One-row-per-match enriched with its card, promotion, event, and location attributes. Useful as a base for most analytics that need match-level slices by date, promotion, event name, or location. | Use for: Count matches by promotion, location, or event over time; Filter matches by wrestler (winner_id/loser_id) and return card metadata; Analyze title changes per promotion or location

views.name: cards_with_promotion_and_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Cards.id AS id,
  Cards.table_id AS table_id,
  Cards.location_id AS location_id,
  Cards.promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  Cards.event_date AS event_date,
  Cards.event_id AS event_id,
  Cards.url AS url,
  Cards.info_html AS info_html,
  Cards.match_html AS match_html,
  Promotions.name AS promotion_name,
  Locations.name AS location_name,
  Events.name AS event_name,
  Tables.html AS table_html,
  Tables.url AS table_url
FROM Cards
LEFT JOIN Promotions ON Cards.promotion_id = Promotions.id
LEFT JOIN Locations ON Cards.location_id = Locations.id
LEFT JOIN Events ON Cards.event_id = Events.id
LEFT JOIN Tables ON Cards.table_id = Tables.id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card enriched with related promotion, location, event, and table display fields — useful for reporting or building further SQL on individual cards.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve card-level metadata and related human-readable names/HTML for display or export (e.g., list all cards with their promotion/location/event/table names). | Filter or group cards by promotion, location, event, or table attributes and then aggregate at the card grain. | Compose additional measures at the card grain (e.g., counts, flags, or joins to single-row dimensions) without changing cardinality.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier of the card — sourced from Cards.id | table_id: foreign key to Tables — sourced from Cards.table_id | location_id: foreign key to Locations — sourced from Cards.location_id | promotion_id: foreign key to Promotions — sourced from Cards.promotion_id | event_date: card's event date/timestamp — sourced from Cards.event_date | event_id: foreign key to Events — sourced from Cards.event_id | url: card-level URL — sourced from Cards.url | info_html: card info HTML blob — sourced from Cards.info_html | match_html: card match HTML blob — sourced from Cards.match_html | promotion_name: promotion display name — sourced from Promotions.name (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | location_name: location display name — sourced from Locations.name (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | event_name: event display name — sourced from Events.name (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | table_html: table-level HTML for the card's table — sourced from Tables.html (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | table_url: table-level URL — sourced from Tables.url (nullable because LEFT JOIN)
params.grounded_columns: Cards.id | Cards.table_id | Cards.location_id | Cards.promotion_id | Cards.event_date | Cards.event_id | Cards.url | Cards.info_html | Cards.match_html | Promotions.id | Promotions.name | Locations.id | Locations.name | Events.id | Events.name | Tables.id | Tables.html | Tables.url
params.metric: This view is purely a projection/enrichment at the card row grain; there are no aggregate metrics defined in the view. | If you need derived measures, compute them on top of this view at the card grain. Example: card_count = COUNT(id) computed by aggregating id over groups.
params.composition: Safe joins (do not duplicate this view's rows/measures): |  - Join to singleton/dimension tables on their primary key (one-to-one or many-to-one) such as Promotions on promotion_id, Locations on location_id, Events on event_id, Tables on table_id — safe because the JOINs in this view are LEFT JOINs to those PKs resulting in at most one matching row per card. |  - Join to other one-row-per-card views (for example, sibling views that are also defined at the same card id grain) on id — safe because they share the same 1:1 cardinality per card id. | Unsafe joins (would multiply rows/measures unless re-aggregated or deduplicated): |  - Do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from card id (for example a hypothetical CardImages, CardEventsLog, or any match-level table that can have multiple rows per card) without first aggregating or deduplicating those rows to one row per card. Such joins will duplicate card rows and thus multiply any card-level measures. |  - Do NOT join to sibling aggregated views that are aggregated at a different grain (e.g., matches_enriched_with_match_type_name if it is at match grain) unless you join on the correct key (event_id or event-level key) and ensure aggregation alignment. | Guidance for planners/composers: |  - If you need metrics that aggregate lower-level rows (one-to-many) related to a card, compute those metrics in a separate subquery or CTE grouped by card id and then LEFT JOIN that aggregated result to cards_with_promotion_and_location on id. This preserves card cardinality and avoids double counting. |  - When joining to event-level or table-level resources, prefer joining on the foreign key present in this view (event_id, table_id, location_id, promotion_id). Because the view contains the foreign keys and the target dimensions are keyed by their id, these joins will not duplicate rows if the target is truly one-row-per-id. |  - If a target view/table may contain multiple rows per the same id (not enforced by PK), first reduce it to one row per id (e.g., via ROW_NUMBER()+FILTER or GROUP BY) before joining.

views.description: One-row-per-card including promotion, location, and event names and the source table URL. Useful for card-level reports, time-series of shows, or joining back to matches for aggregated metrics. | Use for: List cards (shows) with promotion and location details; Find cards scraped from a particular source table URL; Aggregate number of cards per promotion or location over time

views.name: matches_with_wrestler_names
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  w_winner.name AS winner_name,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  w_loser.name AS loser_name,
  m.win_type AS win_type,
  m.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  m.duration AS duration,
  m.title_id AS title_id,
  m.title_change AS title_change
FROM Matches AS m
LEFT JOIN Wrestlers AS w_winner ON CAST(m.winner_id AS TEXT) = CAST(w_winner.id AS TEXT)
LEFT JOIN Wrestlers AS w_loser ON CAST(m.loser_id AS TEXT) = CAST(w_loser.id AS TEXT)

params.description: A one-row-per-match view that returns match identifiers, participating wrestler identifiers and names, and match attributes (win type, match type, duration, title info).
params.when_to_use: List matches for a card including winner/loser display names | Filter or group matches by winner_id/loser_id or winner_name/loser_name | Analyze per-match attributes such as win_type, match_type_id, duration, title_id, and whether a title changed | Compose with card-level or match-type lookups to add card or textual match-type context | Aggregate match-level metrics (counts, average duration) by wrestler, card, match type, or title
params.output_schema: id: match primary key from Matches.id — unique identifier (grain = match.id) | card_id: Matches.card_id — foreign key to the card this match belongs to | winner_id: Matches.winner_id — identifier of the winning wrestler (may be NULL) | winner_name: Wrestlers.name joined from w_winner.name where Wrestlers.id = Matches.winner_id (string, may be NULL) | loser_id: Matches.loser_id — identifier of the losing wrestler (may be NULL) | loser_name: Wrestlers.name joined from w_loser.name where Wrestlers.id = Matches.loser_id (string, may be NULL) | win_type: Matches.win_type — textual or coded description of how the match was decided | match_type_id: Matches.match_type_id — identifier referencing a match type | duration: Matches.duration — match duration as stored in Matches (units per schema) | title_id: Matches.title_id — identifier of title contested in the match (may be NULL) | title_change: Matches.title_change — boolean/flag indicating whether the title changed hands
params.grounded_columns: Matches.id | Matches.card_id | Matches.winner_id | Wrestlers.name (joined as w_winner.name) | Matches.loser_id | Wrestlers.name (joined as w_loser.name) | Matches.win_type | Matches.match_type_id | Matches.duration | Matches.title_id | Matches.title_change
params.metric: row_count = COUNT( matches_with_wrestler_names.id )  -- one row per match (Matches.id) | match_exists_flag = CASE WHEN matches_with_wrestler_names.id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END  -- presence of a match row | match_duration = matches_with_wrestler_names.duration  -- atomic measure: use aggregate (AVG/SUM) when summarizing across rows
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_promotion_and_location on matches_with_wrestler_names.card_id = cards_with_promotion_and_location.id — safe because cards_with_promotion_and_location is one-row-per-card, so joining preserves one-row-per-match (no duplication of match-level measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_enriched_with_match_type_name on matches_with_wrestler_names.id = matches_enriched_with_match_type_name.id — safe when that view is one-row-per-match (it enriches same grain). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_type_lookup on matches_with_wrestler_names.match_type_id = match_type_lookup.id — safe because match_type_lookup is a normalized lookup (one-row-per-match_type_id), so measures remain one-per-match. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_with_card_context on matches_with_wrestler_names.id = matches_with_card_context.id — safe if that sibling view preserves one-row-per-match (do not join if sibling aggregates). | do NOT directly join to card_match_counts (an AGG one-row-per-card) on card_id if you expect to preserve match-level measures without adjustment — joining a one-row-per-card aggregate will duplicate card-level aggregates across all matches of that card unless you instead select the aggregated metric from card_match_counts and treat it as a card-level attribute (which is safe if the planner understands aggregation semantics). | do NOT join to wrestler_aggregate_record (AGG one-row-per-wrestler) without care: joining on winner_id or loser_id will replicate wrestler-level aggregates across each match row for that wrestler (this is safe if your intention is to show wrestler aggregates repeated per-match, but it will multiply any further match-level aggregations unless you re-aggregate appropriately). If you plan to summarize at the wrestler level, aggregate matches_with_wrestler_names first (GROUP BY winner_id or loser_id) before joining to wrestler_aggregate_record. | do NOT join to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., a hypothetical events per match detail table) without re-aggregating those tables to match the match grain — such joins will multiply match rows and invalidate simple SUM/AVG on match measures. | safe composition pattern for aggregation: to compute match-level measures rolled up to another grain (card or wrestler), either (a) aggregate matches_with_wrestler_names first to the target grain (e.g., GROUP BY card_id) and then join to card-level dimensions, or (b) join only to one-row-per-dimension lookup/normalized tables (match_type_lookup, cards_with_promotion_and_location) that do not increase cardinality.

views.description: Match-level rows with resolved winner and loser names from Wrestlers table. Useful when reporting match outcomes by wrestler name rather than id. | Use for: List matches with participant names; Filter matches by wrestler name; Compute per-wrestler win/loss counts

views.name: match_type_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Match_Types.id AS id,
  Match_Types.name AS name,
  CAST(Match_Types.id AS TEXT) AS match_type_id_text
FROM Match_Types

params.description: Provides a canonical lookup of match type identifiers to their display name and a text version of the id.
params.when_to_use: Display or label match_type names where you have Match_Types.id | Join to fact tables (matches) to enrich records with match type name without introducing duplication when matched 1:1 | Compose SQL that needs a text version of match_type id for string operations, partitioning, or joining to external systems that use string ids
params.output_schema: id: numeric identifier of the match type — derived from Match_Types.id | name: human-readable match type name — derived from Match_Types.name | match_type_id_text: textual representation of the match type id — derived from CAST(Match_Types.id AS TEXT)
params.metric: id = Match_Types.id | name = Match_Types.name | match_type_id_text = CAST(Match_Types.id AS TEXT)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_with_card_context on matches_with_card_context.match_type_id = match_type_lookup.id — safe because match_type_lookup is one-row-per-id (grain = ['id']), so joining will not duplicate match_type_lookup rows; the match_type_lookup columns are dimension attributes only. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_with_wrestler_names on matches_with_wrestler_names.match_type_id = match_type_lookup.id — safe for the same reason (one-row-per-match_type id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_enriched_with_match_type_name is typically unnecessary because that view already contains the match type name; avoid redundant joins. | do NOT join match_type_lookup directly to one-to-many aggregate-producing views such as card_match_counts or wrestler_aggregate_record expecting to preserve counts/metrics from those views without re-aggregation — joining a 1:many (match_type_lookup:fact) is fine (it will repeat the single dimension row per fact), but joining a many:1 in the opposite direction (many rows in the other table aggregated at a different grain) can lead to unintended duplication if you then aggregate incorrectly. | If you need to combine match_type_lookup with card_match_counts (an aggregate at card or match granularity), join on the appropriate key in the aggregate (e.g., card_match_counts.match_type_id = match_type_lookup.id) but ensure you aggregate after the join only over the aggregate's grain; do not sum across join-introduced duplicates without grouping by the aggregate's keys. | Avoid joining match_type_lookup to cards_with_promotion_and_location in a way that assumes match_type_lookup will filter or reduce rows — match_type_lookup is purely a dimension and has no measures, so it will only filter/label rows; it will not change metric cardinality unless you apply DISTINCT or GROUP BY on match_type_lookup fields. | Safe composition pattern: SELECT f.*, d.name FROM matches_with_card_context f JOIN match_type_lookup d ON f.match_type_id = d.id — this enriches each match row with the match type name without altering match-level cardinality. | Unsafe-without-care pattern: SELECT d.name, SUM(m.some_metric) FROM match_type_lookup d JOIN matches_with_card_context m ON m.match_type_id = d.id — this is allowed but ensure GROUP BY d.name to avoid duplicating sums due to improper grouping; always aggregate on the fact's grain.

views.description: Normalized mapping of match_type_id to its descriptive name, preserving the match_type_id as stored in Matches. Useful to join into match-level datasets to expose human-readable match type. | Use for: Translate match_type_id in Matches to human-readable names; Group or filter matches by match type name

views.name: matches_enriched_with_match_type_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  m.win_type AS win_type,
  m.match_type_id AS match_type_id,
  mt.name AS match_type_name,
  m.duration AS duration,
  m.title_id AS title_id,
  m.title_change AS title_change
FROM Matches AS m
LEFT JOIN Match_Types AS mt ON CAST(m.match_type_id AS TEXT) = CAST(mt.id AS TEXT)

params.description: Provides one row per match enriched with the match type name from Match_Types, exposing the match's identifiers, participants, outcome, timing, title info, and the human-readable match type.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve match-level details together with the match type name for display, reporting, or further SQL composition. | Filter or group matches by match_type_name while preserving one-row-per-match granularity. | Compose further aggregations (counts, durations, win breakdowns) at the match grain without duplicating match-level measures.
params.output_schema: id: unique match identifier (derived from Matches.id) | card_id: identifier of the card the match belongs to (derived from Matches.card_id) | winner_id: wrestler id who won the match (derived from Matches.winner_id) | loser_id: wrestler id who lost the match (derived from Matches.loser_id) | win_type: coded description of how the match was won (derived from Matches.win_type) | match_type_id: foreign key referencing the match type (derived from Matches.match_type_id) | match_type_name: human-readable name of the match type (derived from Match_Types.name via LEFT JOIN on Match_Types.id) | duration: match duration as stored (derived from Matches.duration) | title_id: identifier of the title contested in the match, if any (derived from Matches.title_id) | title_change: boolean/flag indicating whether the title changed hands (derived from Matches.title_change)
params.grounded_columns: Matches.id | Matches.card_id | Matches.winner_id | Matches.loser_id | Matches.win_type | Matches.match_type_id | Matches.duration | Matches.title_id | Matches.title_change | Match_Types.id | Match_Types.name
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view. All output columns are base columns or direct lookups. If you need counts or sums, derive them by aggregating this view (for example: match_count = COUNT(id); total_duration = SUM(duration)).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_promotion_and_location on card_id = cards_with_promotion_and_location.id — safe because this view is one-row-per-match and cards_with_promotion_and_location is one-row-per-card, so joining preserves a single match row per match and does not duplicate match-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_type_lookup on match_type_id = match_type_lookup.id — safe because match_type_lookup is one-row-per-match_type; joining adds attributes about the match type without duplicating matches. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to matches_with_wrestler_names on id = matches_with_wrestler_names.id — safe because matches_with_wrestler_names is the same grain (one-row-per-match); joining is effectively a horizontal enrichment and will not duplicate rows. | DO NOT join directly to card_match_counts (an aggregate over matches by card) on card_id without considering aggregation semantics if you intend to preserve match-level measures. card_match_counts is one-row-per-card; joining it to this one-row-per-match view is safe from duplication only if you accept the card-level metric being repeated on each match row. If you want to compute match-level measures combined with card-level aggregates without repeating card aggregates, aggregate after joining or join to card_match_counts and then re-aggregate appropriately. | DO NOT join to any one-to-many detail tables (for example, a hypothetical table that lists multiple events per match) without first aggregating that table to the match id. Such joins would multiply match rows and thus duplicate match-level attributes and any derived measures. | If composing higher-level metrics (for example, wins per wrestler), aggregate this view on the desired grouping keys (e.g., winner_id) rather than attempting to join additional one-to-many data into this view and then aggregating — that preserves correctness and avoids accidental double-counting.

views.description: Matches joined to Match_Types to provide the descriptive match type name while preserving the original match_type_id. Useful for aggregations and filters by match type. | Use for: Count matches by match type name; Filter matches using descriptive match type

views.name: card_match_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Matches.card_id AS card_id,
  COUNT(*) AS match_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Matches.title_change = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS title_change_count
FROM Matches
GROUP BY Matches.card_id

params.description: Per-card aggregated counts of matches and how many of those matches included a title change.
params.when_to_use: Get total number of matches per card (event) or how many matches on each card had a title change. | Join as a one-row-per-card measure source when building reports that combine card-level metrics with card attributes (date, location, promotion, title status). | Compose into higher-level aggregates (e.g., promotion-level or wrestler-level summaries) by summing match_count and title_change_count across cards. | Filterable breakdowns by match attributes when joined to normalized match-type or match-duration views — but ensure joins do not duplicate rows.
params.output_schema: card_id: identifier of the card (derived from Matches.card_id). This is the grouping key / grain of the view. | match_count: number of Matches rows for that card (derived from COUNT(*) on Matches rows per card_id). | title_change_count: number of Matches on that card where title_change = 1 (derived from SUM(CASE WHEN Matches.title_change = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)).
params.metric: match_count = COUNT(*) -- count of Matches rows grouped by Matches.card_id | title_change_count = SUM(CASE WHEN Matches.title_change = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) -- count of Matches per card where title_change flag is 1
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_promotion_and_location on card_id — safe because cards_with_promotion_and_location is one-row-per-card (card_id) so this view's per-card measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_time_series on card_id — safe if cards_time_series is one-row-per-card (check that its grain is card_id); joining on matching one-row-per-card preserves match_count/title_change_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_type_lookup or matches_enriched_with_match_type_name only when joining via Matches (i.e., if you need per-match detail) — do NOT directly join this aggregated view to a match-type-to-card one-to-many mapping without re-aggregation, because those joins can duplicate match_count/title_change_count. | DO NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many detail derived from Matches (for example, matches_with_wrestler_names, matches_with_card_context, matches_duration_seconds, wrestler_aggregate_record) without re-aggregating afterwards — those sibling join/normalized views expand Matches rows and will multiplicatively increase match_count/title_change_count if joined without grouping. Instead, either: |   - join this view to one-row-per-card dimensions (cards_with_promotion_and_location, cards_time_series) which preserve cardinality; or |   - join to detailed match-level views (matches_with_wrestler_names, matches_with_card_context, matches_duration_seconds) at the match level (Matches.card_id + match identifier) and then re-aggregate counts from that detailed dataset (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT match_id) or SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) to avoid double-counting. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., promotion-level totals), SUM(match_count) and SUM(title_change_count) across card_id is correct and safe because this view is one-row-per-card and provides additive measures.

views.description: Aggregated counts of matches per card: total matches and number of title changes on the card. Useful for card-level summaries and merging with card metadata. | Use for: Which cards had the most matches; Which cards had title changes and how many

views.name: wrestler_aggregate_record
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w_id AS wrestler_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wins,
  SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS losses,
  SUM(1) AS matches
FROM (
  SELECT winner_id AS w_id, 'win' AS role FROM Matches
  UNION ALL
  SELECT loser_id AS w_id, 'loss' AS role FROM Matches
) AS pooled
GROUP BY w_id

params.description: Per-wrestler counts of match outcomes (wins, losses) and total matches — answers how many matches each wrestler has won, lost, and participated in.
params.when_to_use: Get a roster-level summary of each wrestler's performance (wins, losses, matches) by wrestler_id. | Compose season/period-level aggregates by joining this per-wrestler summary to a time-filtered matches or card view (but re-aggregate or filter correctly — see composition guidance). | Rank or filter wrestlers by total wins, losses, or matches. | Join to wrestler dimension (name/profile) to present readable wrestler-level statistics.
params.output_schema: wrestler_id: the wrestler identifier (derived from Matches.winner_id and Matches.loser_id; aliased as w_id in the subquery and output as wrestler_id) | wins: integer count of matches where this wrestler appears as winner (derived as SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over pooled rows — underlying rows originate from Matches.winner_id) | losses: integer count of matches where this wrestler appears as loser (derived as SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over pooled rows — underlying rows originate from Matches.loser_id) | matches: integer count of all match participations for the wrestler (derived as SUM(1) over pooled rows, effectively wins + losses)
params.metric: wins = SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'win' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- counts occurrences of Matches.winner_id for the wrestler | losses = SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'loss' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) -- counts occurrences of Matches.loser_id for the wrestler | matches = SUM(1)  -- total participations = wins + losses
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a wrestler dimension (e.g., a wrestlers table keyed by wrestler_id) on wrestler_id — safe because this view is one row per wrestler_id, so joining to a one-row-per-wrestler dimension will not duplicate measures. | Safe to join to single-row-per-wrestler views (e.g., wrestlers profile) on wrestler_id — preserves wins/losses/matches without multiplication. | Do NOT join directly to Matches (or any other one-to-many table keyed to wrestler_id) without re-aggregation or de-duplication first — Matches contains one row per match participant and joining it to this one-row-per-wrestler view would multiply the wrestler's aggregated measures (e.g., joining to Matches on wrestler_id would duplicate wins/losses). Instead, either: |   - Filter Matches first to a stricter subset and then re-aggregate to a matching grain (for example, build a new aggregated view scoped to a date range and join on wrestler_id), or |   - Join via a deduplicated single-row-per-match-per-wrestler subquery, then re-aggregate, or | When composing time- or card-scoped metrics (for example, wins in a date range or wins on cards of a certain promotion), do not directly join this global aggregate; instead compute a new aggregate over Matches filtered by date/card/promotion, or join this view to a time/card dimension only if that dimension is one-row-per-wrestler (rare). | Joining to other AGG views that are one-row-per-wrestler is safe (measures align by wrestler_id). | If you need to compute ratios or rates (e.g., win rate), compute them by using the measures from this view (wins / matches) but ensure matches != 0 to avoid division by zero; when deriving such metrics across different grains, perform aggregation at the correct grain first.

views.description: Per-wrestler totals: matches won, matches lost, and total matches (as recorded in Matches). Uses winner_id and loser_id as recorded (TEXT) and preserves those ids for joins back to Wrestlers. | Use for: Leaderboards of wins/losses per wrestler; Compute win percentage (derived downstream) for each wrestler

views.name: cards_time_series
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  promotion_id AS promotion_id,
  event_date AS event_date,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY promotion_id ORDER BY event_date DESC) AS rank_per_promotion
FROM Cards

params.description: Provides a per-card rank (latest-first) within each promotion based on event_date; answers questions about a card's position/order inside its promotion.
params.when_to_use: Find the N most recent or oldest cards per promotion (e.g., top-1 latest card per promotion). | Filter or label cards by their ordinal position inside a promotion (e.g., show only first 3 cards per promotion). | Compose with other card-level data when you need a stable one-row-per-card rank within promotion.
params.output_schema: id: the card primary identifier; derives from Cards.id | promotion_id: the promotion identifier this card belongs to; derives from Cards.promotion_id | event_date: the event date/time of the card; derives from Cards.event_date | rank_per_promotion: integer rank of the card within its promotion ordered by event_date DESC (1 = most recent); derived from ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY promotion_id ORDER BY event_date DESC) computed from Cards.event_date partitioned by Cards.promotion_id
params.metric: rank_per_promotion = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Cards.promotion_id ORDER BY Cards.event_date DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or lookup tables keyed one-to-one to Cards.id or Cards.promotion_id (for example, a promotion lookup view keyed by promotion_id) — safe because cards_time_series is one-row-per Cards.id (grain ['id']) so joining to a one-row-per-promotion dimension on promotion_id will not duplicate rows. | Safe to join to cards_with_promotion_and_location on id (or promotion_id) if that view is one-row-per-card or one-row-per-promotion respectively — confirm the sibling view's grain before joining. | Do NOT join directly to any view or table that is one-to-many from Cards.id (for example, match lists, match events, or any match-level/enriched match view that contains multiple rows per card) without first aggregating the many-side to one row per card. Joining a one-to-many child (matches, match events) will multiply rank_per_promotion and other card-level measures because cards_time_series is one-row-per-card and the child has multiple rows per card. | When composing aggregations: if you need aggregated measures from one-to-many children (e.g., total_matches_per_card from card_match_counts), either (a) join to an aggregated-per-card view (like card_match_counts if it is one-row-per-card), or (b) aggregate after joining using GROUP BY cards_time_series.id to avoid duplicating rank_per_promotion semantics. | Do NOT join to views that are many-to-one in the opposite direction (e.g., multiple promotions per card) because that would indicate inconsistent keys — this view assumes promotion_id is the grouping key used to compute rank_per_promotion. | If you need to compute ranks across additional partition keys, do not rely on rank_per_promotion alone; instead, recompute row_number over the desired partition or filter rows before recomputing to preserve correct cardinality.

views.description: Cards ordered by event_date per promotion, exposing a sequential rank_per_promotion. Useful to select the most recent N cards per promotion downstream by filtering on rank_per_promotion. | Use for: Get latest cards per promotion; Trend analysis of cards over time within a promotion

views.name: matches_duration_seconds
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  duration AS duration,
  CASE
    WHEN duration GLOB '*:*' THEN (
      (CAST(substr(duration, 1, instr(duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60)
      + CAST(substr(duration, instr(duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER)
    )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_seconds
FROM Matches

params.description: Converts a Matches.duration text value of the form 'M:SS' into an integer number of seconds (duration_seconds) and exposes the original duration string per match id.
params.when_to_use: Report or filter on match durations in seconds for individual matches (e.g., find matches shorter/longer than X seconds). | Join as a normalized match-level input when building aggregates that need durations in seconds (e.g., average match length), provided downstream aggregation avoids duplicating match rows. | Compose into time-series or per-card summaries by first aggregating duration_seconds at the match id grain (e.g., SUM(duration_seconds) per card).
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the match row, derived from Matches.id | duration: original duration string as stored, derived from Matches.duration | duration_seconds: integer number of seconds parsed from duration when duration matches the pattern '*:*'; NULL otherwise; computed from Matches.duration
params.metric: duration_seconds = CASE WHEN duration GLOB '*:*' THEN ((CAST(substr(duration, 1, instr(duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60) + CAST(substr(duration, instr(duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER)) ELSE NULL END | duration (passthrough) = Matches.duration | id (grain) = Matches.id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-match (or keyed by Matches.id) such as matches_with_wrestler_names or matches_with_card_context ON id — safe because matches_duration_seconds has one row per Matches.id and these joins are expected to be 1:1, so duration_seconds will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_type_lookup or matches_enriched_with_match_type_name ON match type key (if those views are one-row-per-match or provide a 1:1 mapping) — safe when the right-side is strictly one-row-per-match id. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join to one-to-many children like card_match_counts, wrestler_aggregate_record, or any table/view that is one-to-many per match (e.g., multiple wrestlers per match, multiple events per match) without re-aggregating first, because that will multiply rows and therefore duplicate/overcount duration_seconds if you then SUM or AVG them without first collapsing the match-level measure. | recommended composition pattern for aggregation: to compute aggregates like total or average match duration per card, first join matches_duration_seconds to a one-row-per-match relation that provides card_id (or use Matches.card_id if available), then GROUP BY card_id and apply SUM(duration_seconds) or AVG(duration_seconds) — ensure grouping is performed at the match-id grain before any join to one-to-many detail. | when joining to card-level or wrestler-level aggregates (one-row-per-card or one-row-per-wrestler), either pre-aggregate matches_duration_seconds to that target grain (e.g., SUM(duration_seconds) GROUP BY card_id) or join on match id only when the other side is guaranteed 1:1.

views.description: Normalized match duration converted from MM:SS text to integer seconds where possible. Preserves original duration string. Useful for aggregations on match length and identifying unusually short/long matches. | Use for: Average/median match duration calculations; Filter matches by duration ranges

views.name: matches_with_clean_duration
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS match_id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  m.title_id AS title_id,
  m.title_change AS title_change,
  m.duration AS duration_text,
  -- normalize duration_text into seconds:
  -- handle formats: HH:MM:SS, MM:SS, M:SS, SS, numeric seconds, and ""/NULL filtered outside
  CASE
    WHEN instr(m.duration, ':') > 0 THEN
      -- split by colon from right to support H:MM:SS or MM:SS
      (
        (CASE
           WHEN length(m.duration) - length(replace(m.duration, ':', '')) = 1 THEN
             -- MM:SS
             (cast(substr(m.duration, 1, instr(m.duration, ':')-1) as integer) * 60)
             + cast(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':')+1) as integer)
           ELSE
             -- assume H:MM:SS (two colons) -> hours:minutes:seconds
             (cast(substr(m.duration, 1, instr(m.duration, ':')-1) as integer) * 3600)
             + (cast(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':')+1, instr(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':')+1), ':')-1) as integer) * 60)
             + cast(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':') + 1 + instr(substr(m.duration, instr(m.duration, ':')+1), ':')) as integer)
         END)
      )
    WHEN trim(m.duration) GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN
      cast(m.duration as integer)
    ELSE
      NULL
  END AS duration_seconds
FROM Matches m
WHERE m.duration IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(m.duration) != ''

semantic_filters.duration_text_not_empty: duration IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(duration) != ''

views.description: One row per match with duration parsed/normalized into a canonical time-seconds numeric field and original duration text retained. Filters out NULL/empty duration values so downstream queries can treat duration as a numeric measure.

views.name: matches_with_belt_and_card_context
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id AS match_id,
  m.card_id AS card_id,
  m.winner_id AS winner_id,
  m.loser_id AS loser_id,
  m.title_id AS title_id,
  b.name AS title_name,
  m.title_change AS title_change,
  c.event_date AS event_date,
  c.url AS card_url,
  c.table_id AS table_id
FROM Matches m
LEFT JOIN Belts b ON b.id = m.title_id
LEFT JOIN Cards c ON c.id = m.card_id
views.description: Denormalized match rows joined to belt (title) and card/context information (card date, event/location, table references). Exposes belt id/name and card/event/date to enable filtering and grouping by title and event attributes.

views.name: wrestler_id_name_map
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Wrestlers.id AS wrestler_id,
  Wrestlers.name AS wrestler_name
FROM Wrestlers
views.description: Lookup of wrestler id to canonical name. Useful for resolving winner/loser ids to human-readable names in any match-level result.
